meta.note: Which normative span each SDK restatement was written against, and how that span read when someone last reviewed it. Gate: `spec sdksync`. A pin proves the source is byte-identical to the last review; it does NOT prove the block was correct then. Re-pin with --update only after re-reading. Unpinned blocks are a visible backlog and do not gate.

specs/sdk/SDK-EXTENSION-OPERATIONS.md::Q.why: SA-4: the operator list restated here spelled not-equal `neq`; the normative registry spells it `not_eq`. Loud failure (400 invalid_operator), one debugging session per SDK author.

SA-4: this block restated `entries: [{path, content_hash, entity?}]` with no `has_more` and a mandatory `path`. The normative shape is `matches` of system/query/match, `path` optional per EXTENSION-QUERY §5.4.

specs/sdk/SDK-EXTENSION-OPERATIONS.md::S.why: SA-2 and SA-3, the two worst in the batch and both silent. `events` restated a two-value vocabulary the engine can never match, so a subscription was created, returned an id, and never fired for its lifetime; `rate_limit` restated the unit as per-second against a per-minute normative field, 60x, surfacing on the subscriber as unexplained missing events.
Pinned with SubscribeParams because it echoes the stored subscription entity, and SA-3's diagnosis turned on the fact that it echoes the stored number without the window it will be applied in.
